news.title: Maradona’s ‘Hand of God’ World Cup Ball Sells for Over €2.8 Million at Auction
news.lede: The ball used during Diego Maradona’s famous “Hand of God” goal at the 1986 FIFA World Cup has reportedly been sold at auction for more than €2.8 million, underlining the enduring global appeal of one of football’s most controversial and iconic moments. The historic goal was scored during Argentina’s quarter-final clash against England at the 1986 World Cup in Mexico. Maradona punched the ball into the net ahead of England goalkeeper Peter Shilton, with the goal allowed to stand by the referee. The Argentine football legend later famously described the incident as having been scored “a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God,” giving birth to one of the most memorable phrases in football history.

news.title: Scandal in FIFA: Infantino Wanted to Sell Shares in the World Cup to Trump Relatives
news.lede: The football associations of Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, and the Faroe Islands expressed their lack of confidence in the president of the International Football Federation (FIFA), Gianni Infantino. "The six football associations of the northern countries have lost trust in the FIFA president and are deeply concerned about the leadership style and decisions being made at the highest levels of the organization," their joint statement, released on Sunday, August 23, after a meeting in Helsinki, said. Representatives of the northern countries demanded from FIFA "firm guarantees that it will never open access to its structures and tournaments to private owners." Additionally, the associations stated their loss of confidence in the governing bodies and established procedures within FIFA.

news.title: FIFA hit Argentina with huge fine after Falklands taunt
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. The Argentine FA has been handed a hefty sanction after its players were seen celebrating World Cup victory over England with a banner relating to the Falklands, while various players and staff have been hit with hefty fines for their involvement in the unsavoury scenes which followed the World Cup final. Argentina knocked England out in the tournament semi-finals, and the build-up to the match was dominated by discussions of the Falklands War.

Six Nordic national football associations piled more pressure on embattled FIFA President Gianni Infantino on Sunday by saying they had “lost confidence” in his leadership.

news.title: Ted Lasso Season 4 just broke an Apple TV record. It's the feel-good football fix World Cup fans need
news.lede: The World Cup ended a month ago, but plenty of fans still aren't ready to move on. And judging by the numbers for Ted Lasso Season 4, they aren't the only ones looking for another soccer fix. The show's long-awaited return just delivered the biggest launch in Apple TV history, drawing 296.6 million minutes watched in the U.S. during its first two days of availability, according to Nielsen data supplied by Apple. More than 200 million of those minutes came on Aug. 5 alone, when Ted Lasso was the most-streamed program in the country.

news.title: Nordic nations back calls for Infantino to resign
news.lede: Six Nordic football associations delivered a united blow to Fifa president Gianni Infantino on Sunday, declaring they had lost confidence in his leadership while demanding sweeping governance reforms at world soccer’s governing body. The six Nordic Fifa members — Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden and the Faroe Islands — met in Helsinki and issued a rare joint statement backing calls for Infantino’s resignation from three major regional confederations. The six Nordic football associations have lost confidence in Fifa’s president and are concerned about the organisation’s governance and decision-making at the highest level. They also supported demands for an independent investigation into his controversial proposal to sell a stake in events like the World Cup to private equity investors, a plan that was quickly abandoned in the face of global backlash.

news.title: FIFA Releases 2027 Women’s World Cup Playoff Fixtures
news.lede: The organisers of the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 have confirmed the playoff fixtures, saying six nations will be competing for a place in the Brazil qualification. According to the statement, Ghana and South Africa are among the six nations competing alongside Uzbekistan, Papua New Guinea, Chinese Taipei, and Ecuador. The development was announced on FIFA’s website on Sunday following the meeting held at the body’s headquarters in Zurich on Thursday, August 20, 2026. Sunday Telegraph reports that there are three groups of two teams, with each team scheduled to play three matches.

news.title: Uli Hoeneß says Julian Nagelsmann not solely to blame for Germany’s poor World Cup
news.lede: Uli thinks the problems were beyond Nagelsmann at the World Cup. It already feels like quite some time ago, and yet it also still feels like it was only just a few weeks ago that Germany yet again floundered out of the World Cup far earlier than they should have. In Foxborough, Massachusetts, they fell to Paraguay in a penalty shootout after failing to get the job done in 90 minutes, but the writing was on the wall as they collectively failed to hit their heights throughout the entire tournament — starting off the group stages with a 7-1 trouncing of Curaçao in Houston, Texas probably didn’t do wonders for keeping them on their toes.
